families.page_title: Diphtheria anti-toxin (DAT): information for healthcare professionals
evidence_points: The guidance states that diphtheria antitoxin should be considered urgently for probable and confirmed cases.
It explains that antitoxin is more effective when given early before toxin binds to tissues.
It requires specialist discussion with infectious-disease and UKHSA teams.
It requires continuous monitoring and readiness to manage hypersensitivity including anaphylaxis.
The source is an official GOV.UK primary page from UKHSA or another named UK public authority.
The page was live-opened successfully on 31 July 2026.

The source is specific to urgent specialist use and safe administration of diphtheria antitoxin and should not be generalised beyond its stated population, disease, setting, period or response function.
Operational use requires confirmation of the current page version, responsible organisations, affected people, setting, timing and supporting evidence.
An alert, test result, symptom report, notification, surveillance count or checklist alone does not establish that every recommendation applies.
Final decisions require the current official scope plus exact clinical, laboratory, epidemiological, environmental, operational, communication, governance and review evidence.
